title: La Mesa weighs changes to Flock camera program after millions of license plate scans
byline: Dorian Hargrove • Times of San Diego, Tessa Balc • Times of San Diego
summary: La Mesa Police Department announced it will review its ALPR policy after a Times of San Diego analysis found over 3 million scans on its 20 Flock cameras in seven months due to participation in Flock's statewide network. The department is weighing whether to restrict sharing or leave the state network, and plans to require data-use agreements from outside agencies.

key_quotes.quote: during seven months, from July 1, 2025, through Feb. 2, law enforcement agencies logged more than 3 million scans on the East County city's 20 license plate readers
La Mesa police will reconsider whether to limit which agencies the department shares with or leave Flock's shared network entirely.
The city will soon require outside agencies that use its cameras to sign data-use agreements
